title: publish-release.sh's closing message is hardcoded to 0.3.5 and retired tmux panes
description: scripts/publish-release.sh ends with a quoted heredoc that tells the operator, on EVERY release, to cut a GitHub Release for v0.3.5 using CHANGELOG's [0.3.5] section and to message tmux panes wK:pR and wS:pK, citing LCLI-363's acceptance criteria. All of it is stale: 0.3.5 shipped long ago, LCLI-363 is closed, and pane addressing belongs to the retired Treehouse-era workflow -- sessions are addressed by name via ListAgents now and names change on every restart. Observed live during the 0.6.1 publish on 2026-09-13. The defect is not the wrong values but that they are hardcoded at all: a quoted heredoc cannot interpolate $VERSION, so it was guaranteed to go stale the moment 0.3.5 shipped and will do so again for any fixed version. Fix by deriving the message from $VERSION and removing perishable references (specific task ids, pane addresses) entirely.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The closing message names the version actually being published, derived from $VERSION, so it cannot go stale again
No task id, tmux pane, or fixed version number appears in the closing message
Downstream notification step says to resolve session names with ListAgents rather than naming addresses that change on restart, and includes the opum-marketplace skills/ tree SHA obligation
A manual publish is called out as producing no provenance attestation, since that is now a real possibility per LCLI-482
